---
title: One source. Two views.
---

A twelve-slide feature tour has ten talk slides and two appendix slides. It
shows semantic importance, synchronized code and text, classed equations,
hide-then-dim layering, appendix navigation, footnotes, title emphasis, a
zoomable SVG and inline presenter notes.
**Nocturne** is its declared theme, with automatic light/dark selection in the
source. The links here open fixed light and dark examples.

```{=html}
<div class="home-grid example-links">
<article><span class="eyebrow">Audience</span><h2>Share the slides</h2><p>Outline, navigation and presentation interactions. Actual speaking cues are removed from this file.</p><p><a href="_generated/decks/nocturne/light/index.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open light slides ↗</a> · <a href="_generated/decks/nocturne/dark/index.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Dark slides ↗</a></p></article>
<article><span class="eyebrow">Presenter</span><h2>Keep the cues close</h2><p>The same slides, with a notes panel for each slide. Audience and presenter windows navigate independently.</p><p><a href="_generated/decks/nocturne/light/presenter.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open light presenter ↗</a> · <a href="_generated/decks/nocturne/dark/presenter.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Dark presenter ↗</a></p></article>
</div>
```

## Try the interactions

| Feature | Try it | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Inline title emphasis | [Slide 1](compare.qmd?slide=1) | The word “source” is emphasized; navigation uses plain text. |
| Importance and footnotes | [Slide 3](compare.qmd?slide=3) | Compare key/aside spans and blocks. Follow the footnote and return arrow. |
| Dim layering | [Slide 4](compare.qmd?slide=4) | Advance four times. Future spans and list items stay hidden; past points dim. |
| Code + changing text | [Slide 5](compare.qmd?slide=5) | Advance three times. The highlighted line and matching explanation change together. |
| Equation + changing text | [Slide 6](compare.qmd?slide=6) | Advance three times. Classed math terms and explanations share the same frames. |
| Media | [Slide 7](compare.qmd?slide=7) | Click the diagram to zoom, then press Escape. |
| Speaker notes | [Slide 8](compare.qmd?slide=8) | Choose Presenter with notes to see the actual cue beside the source example. |
| Appendix | [Slide 10](compare.qmd?slide=10) | End/Next stop at 10 / 10. Follow “The supporting data,” visit both appendix slides, and return. |

The appendix reuses the footnote label from slide 3 with independent IDs. Its
second slide inherits appendix status. Press **O** for the overview or use the
outline to jump. Read the [exact semantic syntax](semantic-authoring.md),
including the machine-readable slide-break check.

## Edit the source

```{=html}
<p class="download-links"><a href="_generated/source/index.qmd.txt" download="index.qmd">Download Markdown</a> · <a href="_generated/source/source.css.txt" download="source.css">Download CSS</a> · <a href="_generated/source/two-views.svg" download="two-views.svg">Download SVG</a></p>
```

Save the Markdown as `index.qmd`, the CSS beside it as `source.css`, and the SVG
as `assets/two-views.svg`. The complete editable example is also committed under
`decks/example/` in the repository. Render it with:

```sh
quarto run scripts/htmpres.ts serve decks/example/index.qmd --watch
```

The viewer rebuilds and reloads automatically after saves, keeping the current
slide and audience/presenter view.

The Markdown download includes the public example's speaking cues. See
[the authoring guide](build-a-deck-from-markdown.md) for your own decks, or
[compare this deck across themes](compare.qmd).
